articles.title: Man charged with burglary and voyeurism after allegedly trespassing into high school bathroom, stealing items
articles.description: LONE PEAK, Utah (ABC4) -- A man has been arrested and charged with burglary, voyeurism, and lewdness after he allegedly entered a high school, stole several items, walked into the women's bathroom, and urinated outside. Justin Lane Hopkins, 54, was charged with burglary (a third-degree felony), voyeurism, theft with prior convictions, possession of a dangerous weapon by a restricted person, criminal trespass, lewdness, and littering. According to charging documents, on Aug. 12, Lone Peak Police received a call of a potential trespass at Lone Peak High School. The alleged trespass happened two days earlier, and police claim video footage showed Hopkins entering the school building two separate times on the same day. Reportedly, Hopkins took several items from the building, including an hourglass, a book-shaped box, a can of soda, and a drawstring backpack. Police say the value of the items totaled approximately $500. Then, Hopkins allegedly opened an exterior door of the school and urinated, and shortly after that, he held the door open for someone to enter the building. Police also say that Hopkins entered a women's restroom inside the school twice while events were occurring and while there were people inside the school. Hopkins had previously been trespassed from the school, and signs throughout the building stated that visitors need to check in at the front office. After reviewing the footage, police found Hopkins in an encampment at Highland Glen Park. He allegedly admitted to entering the high school and taking items, and officers found the stolen items in his encampment. They also located a knife, and Hopkins reportedly acknowledged that he was on probation and that he wasn't supposed to have a knife. Police also noticed garbage around the camp, which was in a public park. Hopkins has a history of numerous drug-related convictions dating back to 2012. Most recently, he pleaded guilty to possession of a controlled substance in January 2025. Hopkins is being held in the Utah County Jail with bail. He had his initial court appearance on Monday, Aug. 17, and he has a waiver hearing scheduled for Aug. 26.

pendingReview.title: Safe disposal containers can protect workers from being stuck by a syringe on the job
pendingReview.description: The BDN Opinion section operates independently and does not set news policies or contribute to reporting or editing articles elsewhere in the newspaper or on bangordailynews.com Raymond York is a worker and resident of Presque Isle On the morning of Aug. 5, I was stuck by a discarded syringe while cleaning a public restroom during my shift at a restaurant here in Presque Isle. I washed the wound, notified my manager, drove to Northern Light AR Gould for baseline testing for hepatitis B, hepatitis C and HIV, and filed a report with the Maine Department of Labor. Television station WAGM covered the story also to warn other workers. I am not writing to blame anyone. Addiction is a health issue and our downtown businesses did not create it. I am writing because this is a worker safety issue. Discarded syringes are also being found in other areas of our community -- in parks, in gas station bathrooms, in trash cans. I have talked to other workers who clean those same bathrooms and they have found them too. When you are making $18 an hour taking out trash, you should not have to worry about a needle stick that means months of testing and anxiety. Every needlestick is an OSHA-recordable injury. Every baseline visit can cost $500 or more, even before follow-up testing at six weeks and three months. A locked, puncture-resistant sharps box costs about $60 and a quarterly pickup by a licensed medical waste company can cost less than a single ER bill. Portland, Bangor and Lewiston solved this years ago. City-owned public restrooms are equipped with sharps collection boxes and they provide city-owned and other drop-off boxes and sites where syringes can be disposed of safely, no questions asked. Aroostook County has some safe disposal sites, but we don't have visible boxes where the litter is actually happening. Recently, I went to city hall in Presque Isle to ask the city Council to act. I did not get a chance to speak, so I am asking here. I am asking the City of Presque Isle to do two simple, low-cost things: Add sharps containers to the city's public restroom safety checklist for city buildings and for businesses licensed to have public restrooms; and identify a location and funding source for a 24-hour drop kiosk downtown, using opioid settlement funds where allowable. No one should be stuck with a syringe at work for taking out the trash.

pendingReview.description: Police seized several small wireless cameras and other electronics during the Glassport investigation GLASSPORT, PA - A hidden-camera discovery inside a residential bathroom has led to criminal charges against a 54-year-old man after investigators searched the Glassport home and seized several small wireless cameras and other electronic devices, according to Allegheny County Police. The investigation began Friday, Aug. 14, at about 4:30 p.m., when Glassport Police requested assistance from the Allegheny County Police General Investigations Unit. Small wireless cameras seized County detectives responded to the residence after receiving information about a hidden camera in a bathroom. During the investigation, detectives seized several electronic devices, including multiple small wireless cameras, according to county police. Police did not disclose where each device was allegedly located or provide details about what investigators believe may have been recorded. Information about how the initial camera was discovered was also not released. 54-year-old turns himself in Investigators obtained an arrest warrant for Keith DiMarco, 54, on two counts of violation of privacy. County police said DiMarco subsequently turned himself in. Additional information about his court proceedings was not immediately provided in the police update. The investigation remains subject to change as additional information becomes available. Anyone with information connected to the case can contact the Allegheny County Police Tip Line at 1-833-ALL-TIPS. Callers can remain anonymous. The charges are accusations, and DiMarco is presumed innocent unless proven guilty in court.

pendingReview.title: Brentwood farm worker charged with setting up hidden camera in restroom
pendingReview.description: BRENTWOOD -- A former employee at Frog Hollow Farm has been charged with setting up a hidden camera in a restroom and capturing his female co-workers using the toilet, according to court records. The defendant, Carlos Casas-Tapia, 26, of Brentwood was charged with two misdemeanor counts of invasion of privacy. The charges were filed last March, and Casas-Tapia was sent a notice to appear in court, but things didn't progress from there until just recently, according to court records. After months of waiting, Casas-Tapia is set to have his first court appearance next week, on Aug. 24, records show. The allegations date back to last December, when a woman who works at the farm discovered a hidden camera in the restroom, authorities said. She wrapped it in a towel and called the Contra Costa Sheriff's office. When investigators reviewed footage, they found it had captured multiple women using the restroom and footage where their genitals were exposed, authorities said. But police say the camera also captured something else: Casas-Tapia setting it up. They say the video clearly showed his face as he adjusted it and and placed it toward the toilet, on both Dec. 18 and 19. Other employees told police they were creeped out by Casas-Tapia. It is unclear when he began working at Frog Hollow Farm. Requests to comment from the farm were not immediately returned.

pendingReview.title: Glassport mayor charged after hidden cameras found in home
pendingReview.description: Glassport Mayor Keith DiMarco is in the Allegheny County Jail, arrested for violating a protection-from-abuse order filed by his wife and 22-year-old stepdaughter. Police say they were called after the stepdaughter discovered a hidden camera in her bathroom. Allegheny County Police searched the residence and a day later a PFA was granted, prohibiting DiMarco from contacting his wife. He allegedly left two voicemail messages and also emailed her. A Glassport Borough Council meeting is scheduled Tuesday at 6 p.m. A statement about the situation will be made when the meeting starts. Allegheny County Police say DiMarco faces two count of violation of Privacy.
